- [passage] | Field | Description | Applicable Stages | | --- | --- | --- | | `docsExamined` | Specifies the number of documents scanned during the query execution stage. | `COLLSCAN`, `FETCH` | | `keysExamined` | For query execution stages that scan an index `keysExamined` is the total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys that are examined in the process of the index scan. If the index scan consists of a single contiguous range of keys, only in-bounds keys need to be examined. If the index bounds consists of several key ranges, the index scan execution process may examine out-of-bounds keys in order to skip from the end of one range to the beginning of the next. | `IXSCAN` | | `numReads` | The number of documents scanned or index keys examined during the query execution stage. **New in version 5.1** | `COLLSCAN`, `IXSCAN` | | `seeks` | The number of times that we had to seek the index cursor to a new position in order to complete the index scan. | `IXSCAN` | | `usedDisk` | Whether the stage wrote to disk. **New in version 5.3** | `GROUP` | | `spills` | The number of times the stage spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledBytes` | The total amount of data written to disk in bytes. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledRecords` | The total number of individual records spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledDataStorageSize` | The total disk space, in bytes, used by the spilled data. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `peakTrackedMemBytes` | **New in version 8.3** Maximum number of bytes of tracked memory in use by the current query operation. Starting in MongoDB 9.0, the `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, and `UPDATE` stages also report this field. | `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, `GROUP`, `SORT`, `UPDATE` | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: count, cursor, index, docsExamined, COLLSCAN, FETCH

- [passage] | Option | Description | | --- | --- | | [allUsers](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-allUsers) | Boolean. If set to `false`, `$currentOp` only reports on operations/idle connections/idle cursors/idle sessions belonging to the user who ran the command.; If set to `true`, `$currentOp` reports operations belonging to all users. For standalone and replica sets that enforce access control, `inprog` privilege is required if `allUsers: true`. For sharded clusters that enforce access control, the `inprog` privilege is required to run `$currentOp`. Defaults to `false`. | | [idleConnections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-idleConnections) | Boolean. If set to `false`, `$currentOp` only reports active operations. If set to `true`, `$currentOp` returns all operations, including idle connections. Defaults to `false`. | | [idleCursors](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-idleCursors) | Boolean. If set to `true`, `$currentOp` reports on cursors that are "idle"; i.e. open but not currently active in a [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) operation. Information on idle cursors have the [`type`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.type) set to `"idleCursor"`. Information on cursors currently active in a [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) operation information have the [`type`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.type) set to `"op"` and [`op`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.op) set to `getmore`. Defaults to `false`. | | [idleSessions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-idleSessions) | Boolean. If set to `true`, in addition to active/dormant operations, `$currentOp` reports on:Inactive sessions that are holding locks as part of a transaction. Each inactive session appears as a separate document in the `$currentOp` stream.The document for a session includes information on the session ID in the [`lsid`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.lsid) field and the transaction in the [`transaction`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.transaction) field.Information on idle sessions have the [`type`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.type) set to `"idleSession"`.; [`$currentOp.twoPhaseCommitCoordinator`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.twoPhaseCommitCoordinator) in `inactive` [`state`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.twoPhaseCommitCoordinator.state); If set to `false`, `$currentOp` doesn't report on:Inactive sessions; [`$currentOp.twoPhaseCommitCoordinator`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.twoPhaseCommitCoordinator) information in `inactive` [`state`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.twoPhaseCommitCoordinator.state) Defaults to `true`. | | [localOps](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-localOps) | Boolean. If set to `true` for an aggregation running on [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), `$currentOp` reports only operations running locally on that [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos). If `false`, then `$currentOp` instead reports operations running on the shards. The `localOps` parameter has no effect for `$currentOp` aggregations running on [`mongod`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) Defaults to `false`. | | [targetAllNodes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-targetAllNodes) | Boolean. If set to `true`, `$currentOp` outputs a document for each data-bearing node for all shards. If set to `false`, `$curentOp` outputs a document for each shard. For example, in a sharded cluster with three shards where each shard is a replica set with three nodes: `targetAllNodes=false` outputs three documents; `targetAllNodes=true` outputs nine documents Defaults to `false`. **New in version 7.1** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#syntax · keywords: cursor, sharded query targeting, false, $currentOp, true, inprog

- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `cursor` | Contains the cursor information, including the cursor ID and the `nextBatch` of documents. If [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) (or subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands) returns partial results because the queried shard(s) aren't available, the [find output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-cmd-find-output) includes a `partialResultsReturned` indicator field. If the queried shards are available for the initial `find` command, but one or more shards become unavailable for subsequent `getMore` commands, only the `getMore` commands that run while the shards aren't available include `partialResultsReturned` in their output. The `postBatchResumeToken` field can be used with the [`$changeStream`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/changestream.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-changeStream) pipeline to start or resume a change stream from this point. Starting in MongoDB 9.0, you can set the [`internalOperationResponseMaxMS`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.internalOperationResponseMaxMS) parameter to return an updated `postBatchResumeToken` during a long change stream oplog scan, before the command fills a batch or the change stream reaches the end of the oplog. | | `"ok"` | Indicates whether the command has succeeded (`1`) or failed (`0`). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getMore.md#output · keywords: cursor, nextBatch, find, getMore, partialResultsReturned, postBatchResumeToken · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md
- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `samplingRate` | The sampling rate used to mirror a subset of [operations that support mirroring](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/replication.md#std-label-mirrored-reads-supported-operations) to a subset of electable (specifically, [`priority greater than 0`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.priority)) secondaries. That is, the primary mirrors reads to each electable secondary at the specified sampling rate. Valid values are: `0.0`Turns off mirroring.`1.0`The primary mirrors all [operations that support mirroring](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/replication.md#std-label-mirrored-reads-supported-operations) to each electable secondary.Number between `0.0` and `1.0` (exclusive)The primary randomly samples each electable secondary at the specified rate to be sent mirrored reads. For example, given a replica set with a primary and two electable secondaries and a sampling rate of `0.10`, the primary mirrors reads to each electable secondary at the sampling rate of 10 percent such that one read may be mirrored to one secondary and not to the other or to both or to neither. That is, if the primary receives `100` operations that can be mirrored, the sampling rate of `0.10` may result in `8` reads being mirrored to one secondary and `13` reads to the other or `10` to each, etc. The default value is `0.01`. | | `maxTimeMS` | The maximum time in milliseconds for the mirrored reads. The default value is `1000`. The `maxTimeMS` for the mirrored reads is separate from the `maxTimeMS` of the original read being mirrored. | | `targetedMirroring` | Contains fields to configure how you target specific nodes for cache warming. For more information on targeted mirroring, see [Targeted Mirrored Reads.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/replication.md#std-label-targeted-mirrored-reads) Includes the following fields: `tag`Defaults to an empty `BSONObj`. The [replica set tag](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/configure-replica-set-tag-sets.md#std-label-replica-set-configuration-tag-sets) that you can use to target nodes for mirroring. You can configure a node for targeted mirroring using the following syntax:`tag: { "<tag1>": "<string1>" }`You can only supply one tag. All nodes within the same replica set that have these tags are targeted.`samplingRate`*Type*: Float*Range*: `0.0` to `1.0` (inclusive)The rate at which targeted reads are mirrored to the host or hosts. A rate of `0.0` means no reads are mirrored, and a rate of `1.0` means all reads are mirrored. Although `samplingRate` defaults to `0.01`, the `targetedMirroring` feature is off by default, since the `tag` field defaults to empty.`maxTimeMS`*Type*: intThe maximum time in milliseconds before the mirrored read times out. The minimum value for `maxTimeMS` is `0`. Defaults to `1000`. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#replication-and-consistency · keywords: cursor, samplingRate, priority greater than 0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.10

- [passage] MongoDB omits counters with a count of zero and omits subdocuments that contain no counters. If none of the recorded queries produced plan shape counters, MongoDB omits the planShapeCounters document entirely. For example, a query that matches a single document by _id uses a fast path that doesn't match any tracked plan shape, so its query stats entry contains no planShapeCounters document. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: count · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] - A `count` field that contains the number of documents in the bucket. The `count` field is included by default when the `output` document is not specified. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucketAuto.md#definition · keywords: count, output
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `groupBy` | expression | An [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) to group documents by. To specify a [field path](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline.md#std-label-agg-quick-ref-field-paths), prefix the field name with a dollar sign `$` and enclose it in quotes. | | `buckets` | integer | A positive 32-bit integer that specifies the number of buckets into which input documents are grouped. | | `output` | document | Optional. A document that specifies the fields to include in the output documents in addition to the `_id` field. To specify the field to include, you must use [accumulator expressions:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/accumulators.md#std-label-agg-quick-reference-accumulators) `<outputfield1>: { <accumulator>: <expression1> }, ...` The default `count` field is not included in the output document when `output` is specified. Explicitly specify the `count` expression as part of the `output` document to include it: `output: { <outputfield1>: { <accumulator>: <expression1> }, ... count: { $sum: 1 } }` | | `granularity` | string | Optional. A string that specifies the [preferred number series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preferred_number) to use to ensure that the calculated boundary edges end on preferred round numbers or their powers of 10. Available only if the all `groupBy` values are numeric and none of them are `NaN`. The supported values of `granularity` are: `"R5"`, `"R10"`, `"R20"`, `"R40"`, `"R80"`, `"1-2-5"`, `"E6"`, `"E12"`, `"E24"`, `"E48"`, `"E96"`, `"E192"`, and `"POWERSOF2"`. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucketAuto.md#definition · keywords: count, groupBy,  and enclose it in quotes. | | , output, _id, <outputfield1>: { <accumulator>: <expression1> }, ...
- [passage] You can apply `$unwind` multiple times in a single pipeline to expand documents that contain several array fields. The following operation unwinds the `genres` array and then the `cast` array to produce a flat document for every genre-actor combination, then groups by genre to count the total cast appearances in each genre: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unwind.md#unwind-multiple-array-fields · keywords: count, $unwind, genres, cast
- [passage] Messages related to database commands, such as count. To specify the log level for COMMAND components, use the systemLog.component.command.verbosity setting. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: count
- [passage] This section contains examples that use a cursor to read documents from a collection with temperature readings from a weather sensor. You'll see examples of `isExhausted()`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.isExhausted.md#examples · keywords: cursor, isExhausted()

## How it works

- [passage] If you include a [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) that specifies a [sparse index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) when you perform a [`count()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#mongodb-method-cursor.count) of all documents in a collection (i.e. with an empty query predicate), the sparse index is used even if the sparse index results in an incorrect count. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-and-incomplete-results · keywords: count, cursor, index, query shape, hint(), count()
- [passage] When you call [`count()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#mongodb-method-cursor.count) on a [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operation which does not specify a query predicate, the [`count()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#mongodb-method-cursor.count) method can return inaccurate document counts. These [`count()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#mongodb-method-cursor.count) methods return results based on the collection's metadata, which may result in an approximate count. In particular, — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#inaccurate-counts-without-query-predicate · keywords: count, cursor, query shape, count(), find()
- [passage] On a sharded cluster, [`count()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#mongodb-method-cursor.count) without a query predicate in the `find` can result in an *inaccurate* count if [orphaned documents](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-orphaned-document) exist or if a [chunk migration](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration.md#std-label-sharding-balancing) is in progress. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#sharded-clusters · keywords: count, cursor, query shape, count(), find · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.count.md
- [passage] - When an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) exists for the query shape, MongoDB ignores the [`hint()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#behavior · keywords: cursor, index, query shape, hint()
- [passage] The [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) typically selects the optimal index for a specific operation. However, you can force MongoDB to use a specific index using the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method. Use [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) to support performance testing or when you are querying a field that appears in several indexes to ensure that MongoDB uses the correct index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#use-index-hints · keywords: cursor, index, query optimization, hint()
- [fact] Every read preference mode except primary may return stale data because secondaries replicate asynchronously. maxStalenessSeconds lets the client skip secondaries whose estimated lag is too high. The modes secondary and secondaryPreferred compare lag with the primary; primaryPreferred and nearest compare with the freshest secondary when there is no primary. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-preference.md · keywords: cursor, read preference, Cursor and Read-Path Tuning (batchSize and maxTimeMS and read preference)
- [passage] [`itcount()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.itcount.md#mongodb-method-cursor.itcount) is similar to [`cursor.count()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#mongodb-method-cursor.count), but actually executes the query on an existing iterator, exhausting its contents in the process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.itcount.md#definition · keywords: count, cursor, itcount(), cursor.count()
- [passage] [`min()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#mongodb-method-cursor.min) exists primarily to support the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#definition · keywords: cursor, sharded query targeting, min(), mongos
- [passage] This point-in-time value is distinct from [`metrics.changeStreams.cursor.totalOpened`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus.md#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.metrics.changeStreams.cursor.totalOpened), which is a cumulative count. Use this value to assess how heavily change streams use this process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: count, cursor, metrics.changeStreams.cursor.totalOpened
- [passage] [`max()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#mongodb-method-cursor.max) exists primarily to support the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) (sharding) process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#parameters · keywords: cursor, sharded query targeting, max(), mongos
- [passage] The [MongoCollection.find()](https://mongodb.github.io/mongo-java-driver/5.11/apidocs/driver-kotlin-coroutine/mongodb-driver-kotlin-coroutine/com.mongodb.kotlin.client.coroutine/-mongo-collection/find.html) method returns an instance of the [FindFlow](https://mongodb.github.io/mongo-java-driver/5.11/apidocs/driver-kotlin-coroutine/mongodb-driver-kotlin-coroutine/com.mongodb.kotlin.client.coroutine/-find-flow/index.html) class. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#cursor · keywords: cursor, index
- [passage] When specifying [`linearizable read concern`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-), always use [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) in case a majority of data bearing members are unavailable. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.readConcern.md#linearizable-read-concern-performance · keywords: cursor, read preference, linearizable read concern, maxTimeMS()
- [passage] For sharded clusters, mongos applies the read preference when reading from the shards. The member selected is governed by both the read preference and replication.localPingThresholdMs settings, and is re-evaluated for each operation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: read preference, sharded query targeting
- [passage] Views are the result of aggregation pipelines. When you use $sample on a view, MongoDB appends the stage to the end of the view's aggregation pipeline syntax. Therefore, the $sample stage on a view is never the first stage and always results in a collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample/ · keywords: count, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample.md
- [passage] Because index filters override the expected behavior of the planner as well as the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method, use index filters sparingly. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: cursor, index, hint()
- [passage] When executing [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) queries with a [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort), MongoDB can use indexes that support the [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) clauses. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#or-and-sort-operations · keywords: cursor, index, $or, sort()
- [passage] - Use an index to satisfy the sort so that MongoDB doesn't sort documents in memory. To learn more, see [Sort and Index Use.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-index-use) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#per-operation-memory-limit · keywords: cursor, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] Setting [`cursorTimeoutMillis`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.cursorTimeoutMillis) to less than or equal to `0` results in all cursors being immediately eligible for timeout. Generally, the timeout value should be greater than the average amount of time for a query to return results. Use tools like the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) cursor modifier to analyze the average query time and select an appropriate timeout period. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: cursor, index, cursorTimeoutMillis, cursor.explain()
- [passage] When possible, [`db.collection.distinct()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.distinct.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.distinct) operations can use indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.distinct.md#index-use · keywords: count, index, db.collection.distinct()
- [passage] Specifies the *inclusive* lower bound for a specific index in order to constrain the results of [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find). [`min()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#mongodb-method-cursor.min) provides a way to specify lower bounds on compound key indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#definition · keywords: cursor, index, find(), min()
- [passage] Because [`min()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#mongodb-method-cursor.min) requires an index on a field, and forces the query to use this index, you may prefer the [`$gte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gte.md#mongodb-query-op.-gte) operator for the query if possible. Consider the following example: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#interaction-with-index-selection · keywords: cursor, index, min(), $gte
- [passage] The [change streams](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams/) cursors that the MongoDB Search process (`mongot`) uses to keep MongoDB Search indexes updated can contribute to the query targeting ratio and trigger [query targeting alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md#std-label-query-targeting-alerts) if the ratio is high. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#common-triggers · keywords: cursor, index, mongot · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/
- [passage] Specifies the *exclusive* upper bound for a specific index in order to constrain the results of [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find). [`max()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#mongodb-method-cursor.max) provides a way to specify an upper bound on compound key indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#definition · keywords: cursor, index, find(), max()
- [passage] Because [`max()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#mongodb-method-cursor.max) requires an index on a field, and forces the query to use this index, you may prefer the [`$lt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lt.md#mongodb-query-op.-lt) operator for the query if possible. Consider the following example: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#interaction-with-index-selection · keywords: cursor, index, max(), $lt
- [passage] | Counter | Description | | --- | --- | | `collscan``clusteredCollscan` | Collection scans, counted separately based on whether the scan uses the [clustered index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#std-label-clustered-collections) | | `coveredIxscan` | Index scans that don't fetch documents. | | `ixscanFetch` | Index scans that fetch documents. | | `countScan` | Scans that count index keys without returning documents. | | `distinctScan``distinctScanFetch` | Scans that skip duplicate index keys, counted separately based on whether the scan fetches documents. | | `geoNear2d``geoNear2dSphere` | Geospatial proximity searches, counted separately based on whether the query uses a [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index) or [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) index. | | `textMatch` | Text searches that use a [text index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) | | `otherAccessPath` | Winning plans that don't use a collection scan, an index scan, a count scan, a distinct scan, or a geospatial access path. A plan that only performs a text search increments both `textMatch` and `otherAccessPath`. | | `btreeIxscan``wildcardIxscan``sparseIxscan``uniqueIxscan``hashedIxscan``multikeyIxscan` | Index scans, counted separately by index property. A single index scan can increment multiple of these counters. | | `boundsFullScan``boundsPoint``boundsBoundedRange``boundsMinKeyToValue``boundsValueToMaxKey``boundsMixture` | Index scans, counted separately by the index bounds that the scan uses. MongoDB increments `boundsMixture` when the scan uses more than one type of bound. | | `boundsUnionedSmall``boundsUnionedLarge` | Index scans where a field has multiple bounds, counted separately by the number of bounds. `boundsUnionedSmall` counts fields with 2 to 50 bounds, and `boundsUnionedLarge` counts fields with 51 or more bounds. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md#access-path-counters · keywords: count, index, collscan, clusteredCollscan, coveredIxscan, ixscanFetch
- [passage] The time reported by `explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis` is not necessarily representative of actual query time. During steady state operations (when the query plan is cached), or when using [`cursor.hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) with `cursor.explain()`, MongoDB bypasses the plan selection process, resulting in a faster actual time, leading to a lower `explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis` value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: cursor, index, explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis, cursor.hint(), cursor.explain() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] The number of times that we had to seek the index cursor to a new position in order to complete the index scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: cursor, index
- [statement] A filtered count is covered when an index holds all filter fields; verify with explain('executionStats') showing a COUNT_SCAN stage and totalDocsExamined: 0. — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-index-for-count-operations/markdown · keywords: count, index, Count and Distinct and Sampling Optimization
- [passage] When you call [`count`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.count) without a query predicate, you may receive inaccurate document counts. Without a query predicate, [`count`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.count) commands return results based on the collection's metadata, which may result in an approximate count. In particular, — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md#inaccurate-counts-without-query-predicate · keywords: count, query shape
- [passage] - If you use the [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) method in your query, MongoDB performs a second sort operation, re-ordering the matching documents. When querying large collections, this can negatively affect query performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nearSphere.md#sort-operation · keywords: cursor, query optimization, sort() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/near.md
- [passage] Without a query predicate, `count()` returns results based on the collection's metadata, which may result in an incorrect count. - [passage] `$clusterTime` is the timestamp from the [oplog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-oplog.md#std-label-replica-set-oplog) entry when the `cakeSales` collection is modified. See [Command Response.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.runcommand.md#std-label-command-response) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/tsIncrement.md#use-tsincrement-in-a-change-stream-cursor-to-monitor-collection-changes · keywords: cursor, $clusterTime, cakeSales · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/tsSecond.md
- [passage] | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | [`$accumulator`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md#mongodb-group-grp.-accumulator) | Returns the result of a user-defined accumulator function. | | [`$addToSet`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/addtoset.md#mongodb-group-grp.-addToSet) | Returns an array of *unique* expression values for each group. Order of the array elements is undefined. | | [`$avg`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/avg.md#mongodb-group-grp.-avg) | Returns an average of numerical values. | | [`$bottom`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bottom.md#mongodb-group-grp.-bottom) | Returns the bottom element within a group according to the specified sort order. | | [`$bottomN`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bottomn.md#mongodb-group-grp.-bottomN) | Returns an aggregation of the bottom `n` fields within a group, according to the specified sort order. | | [`$concatArrays`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/concatarrays.md#mongodb-group-grp.-concatArrays) | Returns a single array that combines the elements of two or more arrays. **New in version 8.1** | | [`$count`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/count-accumulator.md#mongodb-group-grp.-count) | Returns the number of documents in a group. Only meaningful when documents are in a defined order. Distinct from the [`$firstN`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/expression/firstn.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-firstN) array operator. | | [`$last`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/last.md#mongodb-group-grp.-last) | Returns the result of an [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) for the last document in a group. | | [`$lastN`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lastn.md#mongodb-group-grp.-lastN) | Returns the result of evaluating a specified expression over the last n elements in a group. | | [`$max`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/max.md#mongodb-group-grp.-max) | Returns the highest expression value for each group. | | [`$maxN`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/maxn.md#mongodb-group-grp.-maxN) | Returns an aggregation of the `n` maximum valued elements in a group. Distinct from the [`$maxN`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/maxn-array-element.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-maxN) array operator. | | [`$median`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/median.md#mongodb-group-grp.-median) | Returns an approximation of the median (50th [percentile](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-percentile)) value of documents in a group. **New in version 7.0** | | [`$mergeObjects`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/mergeobjects.md#mongodb-group-grp.-mergeObjects) | Returns a document created by combining the input documents for each group. | | [`$min`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/min.md#mongodb-group-grp.-min) | Returns the lowest expression value for each group. | | [`$minN`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/minn.md#mongodb-group-grp.-minN) | Returns an aggregation of the `n` minimum valued elements in a group. Distinct from the [`$minN`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/expression/minn-array-element.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-minN) array operator. | | [`$percentile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/percentile.md#mongodb-group-grp.-percentile) | Returns an array of scalar values that correspond to specified [percentile](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-percentile) values. **New in version 7.0** | | [`$push`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/push.md#mongodb-group-grp.-push) | Returns an array of expression values for documents in each group. | | [`$setUnion`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/setunion.md#mongodb-group-grp.-setUnion) | Takes two or more arrays and returns an array containing the elements that appear in any input array. **New in version 8.1** | | [`$stdDevPop`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/stddevpop.md#mongodb-group-grp.-stdDevPop) | Returns the population standard deviation of values from documents in a group. | | [`$stdDevSamp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/stddevsamp.md#mongodb-group-grp.-stdDevSamp) | Returns the sample standard deviation of values from documents in a group. | | [`$sum`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sum.md#mongodb-group-grp.-sum) | Returns a sum of numerical values. Ignores non-numeric values. | | [`$top`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/top.md#mongodb-group-grp.-top) | Returns the top element within a group according to the specified sort order. | | [`$topN`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/topn.md#mongodb-group-grp.-topN) | Returns an aggregation of the top `n` fields within a group, according to the specified sort order. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#accumulator-operator · keywords: count, $accumulator, $addToSet, $avg, $bottom, $bottomN

- [passage] - Set the value substantially higher than the change stream's `maxTimeMS` or `maxAwaitTimeMS` value, but lower than the network timeout value. - [passage] A document that reports the number of change stream cursors currently open in this process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: cursor
- [passage] This value is always less than or equal to [`metrics.changeStreams.cursor.open.total`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus.md#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.metrics.changeStreams.cursor.open.total), because open cursors can be idle. - [passage] - When using the [`$collStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collstats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-collStats) stage, only the `count` field is available. All other [`$collStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collstats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-collStats) fields are not available in Stable API V1. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#stable-api · keywords: count, $collStats
- [passage] Marks the cursor as [tailable](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/tailable-cursors.md#std-label-tailable-cursors-landing-page) keeping it open even when the client exhausts all results. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.tailable.md#definition · keywords: cursor
- [passage] If `awaitData` is `true`, when the cursor reaches the end of the capped collection, [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-program-mongod) blocks the query thread for the timeout interval and waits for new data to arrive. When new data is inserted into the capped collection, `mongod` signals the blocked thread to wake and return the next batch to the client. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.tailable.md#behavior · keywords: cursor, awaitData, true, mongod
- [passage] The MongoDB instance returns response in batches. To retrieve all the documents from a cursor may require multiple batch responses from the MongoDB instance. When there are no more documents remaining in the current batch, the cursor will retrieve another batch to get more documents until the cursor exhausts. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.objsLeftInBatch.md · keywords: cursor
- [passage] - Because the 31st is a Sunday and it is between `startDate` and `endDate`, one `week` is added to the count. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateDiff.md#weeks-per-month · keywords: count, startDate, endDate, week
- [passage] - The `week` count is incremented even when a calendar week finishes after `endDate` or in the next calendar period. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateDiff.md#weeks-per-month · keywords: count, week, endDate
- [passage] The Query Profiler samples operations by using a bucketing algorithm that adjusts the sample size based on the width of the selected time range. Because of differences in bucket size, a wider time range might display fewer sampled operations than a narrower time range. For exact, unsampled operation counts, download your `mongod` logs. To learn more, see [View and Download MongoDB Logs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/mongodb-logs.md#std-label-mongodb-logs) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#data-display-limitations · keywords: count, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] - If the deployment is a sharded cluster, a shard removal may cause an open change stream cursor to close. The closed change stream cursor may not be fully resumable. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#behavior · keywords: cursor
- [passage] The [Mongo::Collection#find()](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ruby-driver/current/api/Mongo/Collection.html#find-instance_method) method returns a [CollectionView](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ruby-driver/current/api/Mongo/Collection/View.html), which is an `Enumerable`. A [Cursor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ruby-driver/current/api/Mongo/Cursor.html) is created when the `View` is enumerated; for example, by calling `#to_a()` or `#each()`. You can also get an `Enumerator` by calling `#to_enum()` on the `View`. See the Ruby driver API documentation for [iterating over a cursor.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ruby-driver/current/api/Mongo/Cursor.html#each-instance_method) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#cursor · keywords: cursor, Enumerable, View, #to_a(), #each(), Enumerator
- [passage] When you run a find operation with a MongoDB driver or `mongosh`, MongoDB returns a [cursor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/cursors.md#std-label-cursors) that manages query results. Query results are not returned as an array of documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#query-result-format · keywords: cursor, mongosh
- [passage] You can use `isExhausted()` with a [tailable cursor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/tailable-cursors.md#std-label-tailable-cursors-landing-page). A tailable cursor stays open even if no documents remain in the current batch. Other cursors are automatically closed when no documents remain. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.isExhausted.md#tailable-cursors · keywords: cursor, isExhausted()
- [passage] The following example adds the `DBQuery.Option.tailable` flag and the `DBQuery.Option.awaitData` flag to ensure that the query returns a [tailable cursor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/tailable-cursors.md#std-label-tailable-cursors-landing-page). The sequence creates a cursor. After returning the full result set, it waits for the default interval of 1000 milliseconds so that it can capture and return additional data added during the query: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.addOption.md#example · keywords: cursor, DBQuery.Option.tailable, DBQuery.Option.awaitData

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To obtain the correct count of the number of documents in the `movies` collection, do not [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) with a [sparse index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) when performing a count of all documents in a collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-and-incomplete-results · keywords: count, cursor, index, movies, hint()
- [passage] To see whether MongoDB will apply an index filter for a plan cache query shape, check the [`indexFilterSet`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.indexFilterSet) field of either the [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#set-filter-on-plan-cache-query-shape-consisting-of-predicate-only · keywords: cursor, index, query shape, indexFilterSet, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain()
- [passage] To target secondaries with specific tags, include both the [mode](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.readpref.md#std-label-cursor-readpref-mode) and the [tagSet](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.readpref.md#std-label-cursor-readpref-tagset) array: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.readPref.md#specify-read-preference-tag-set · keywords: cursor, read preference
- [passage] Use read isolation to improve consistency. To learn more, see [Read Concern `"snapshot"`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md#std-label-read-concern-snapshot) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-isolation-consistency-recency.md#cursor-snapshot · keywords: cursor, read preference, "snapshot"
- [passage] To override the default read concern level, use the `readConcern` option. The [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) command uses the `readConcern` level specified in the originating [`aggregate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.aggregate) command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md#override-readconcern · keywords: cursor, read preference, readConcern, getMore, aggregate · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md
- [passage] To see whether your operation results in a `DISTINCT_SCAN`, check your operation's [explain results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#retrieve-distinct-values · keywords: count, index, DISTINCT_SCAN
- [passage] To view the query plan information for a given query, you can use [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) . — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#query-plan-and-cache-information · keywords: cursor, index, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain()
- [passage] Use the [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method in [executionStats](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-executionStats) mode to return statistics about the query process, including the index used, the number of documents scanned, and the time the query takes to process in milliseconds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#return-query-plan-with-explain · keywords: cursor, index, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md
- [passage] Run [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method in [allPlansExecution](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-allPlansExecution) mode to view partial execution statistics collected during plan selection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#return-query-plan-with-explain · keywords: cursor, index, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain()
- [passage] To view the execution statistics for a specific index, append to the [`db.collection.find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method followed by [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain), e.g.: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#control-index-use-with-hint · keywords: cursor, index, db.collection.find(), hint(), cursor.explain()
- [passage] Use `$natural` in conjunction with `cursor.hint()` to perform a collection scan to return documents in [natural order.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-natural-order) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#natural · keywords: cursor, index, $natural, cursor.hint()
- [passage] To force MongoDB to use a particular index, use cursor.hint() (mongosh method) when testing indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: cursor, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md
- [passage] To use an index with the [`max()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#mongodb-method-cursor.max) method, you must use the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method to specify the index you want to use, except when the [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) query is an equality condition on the `_id` field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#definition · keywords: cursor, index, max(), hint(), find(), _id · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md
- [passage] To confirm whether a query used an index, run the query with the [`explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) option. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md#create-indexes-with-collation · keywords: cursor, index, explain()
- [passage] To view the query plan selected, chain the [`cursor.explain("executionStats")`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) cursor method to the end of the **find** command: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: cursor, index, cursor.explain("executionStats") · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/

## Measurements and reference values

- [passage] | Chart | Description | | --- | --- | | Connections | Number that indicates the total active connections to the cluster. Monitor connections to determine whether the current connection limits are sufficient. If necessary, scale the cluster tier. To learn more, see [Fix Connection Issues](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/connection-alerts.md#std-label-connection-alerts) and [Fix Lost Primary.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/no-primary.md#std-label-no-primary) Use [`$currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-currentOp) to determine which collections are using more connections in a cluster. For more details, see [Count Collection Connections.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp/#count-collection-connections) | | Disk IOPS | Number that indicates the input operations per second. Monitor whether disk IOPS approaches the maximum provisioned IOPS. Determine whether the cluster can handle future workloads. To learn more, see [Fix IOPS Issues](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/disk-io-utilization.md#std-label-disk-io-util) and [Fix Lost Primary.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/no-primary.md#std-label-no-primary) | | Disk Usage | Number that indicates the total bytes of used disk space for the cluster. Monitor the combined size of your data and MongoDB operational data (buffer, journal, and log files) on the cluster. IMPORTANT: The UI displays GB, but all disk usage metrics are in gibibytes (GiB). To learn more, see [Fix Storage Issues.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/disk-space-used.md#std-label-disk-space-used) | | Query Targeting | Number that indicates the efficiency of read operations run on MongoDB. Monitor query targeting metrics to identify inefficient queries. The [change streams](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams/) cursors that the MongoDB Search process (`mongot`) uses to keep MongoDB Search indexes updated can contribute to the query targeting ratio and trigger [query targeting alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md#std-label-query-targeting-alerts) if the ratio is high. To learn more, see [Fix Query Issues.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#std-label-query-targeting-resolution) | | Normalized System CPU | Number that indicates CPU usage of all processes on the node, scaled to a range of 0-100% by dividing by the number of CPU cores. Monitor CPU usage to determine whether to scale to a higher cluster tier. If you are unable to see the usage that triggered the alert, zoom in on the Normalized System CPU chart by clicking and dragging your mouse over the period of interest. With a higher-resolution view you may be able to identify acute spikes in CPU usage that weren't visible in the overview. To learn more, see [Fix IOPS Issues](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/disk-io-utilization.md#std-label-disk-io-util), [Fix Lost Primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/no-primary.md#std-label-no-primary), and [Fix CPU Usage Issues.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/system-cpu-usage.md#std-label-system-cpu) | | Oplog GB/Hour | Number that indicates the average rate in gigabytes of [oplog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-oplog) data that the primary generates per hour. Monitor oplog data to determine whether you have to increase the oplog size. To learn more, see [Fix Oplog Issues.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/replication-oplog.md#std-label-replication-oplog-alerts) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/monitor-cluster-metrics.md#important-metrics · keywords: count, cursor, index, $currentOp, mongot
- [fact] $sample uses a pseudo-random cursor only if it is the first pipeline stage, N is under 5% of the collection (threshold not configurable), and the collection has more than 100 documents. Otherwise it reads all input and does a top-k random sort, which is subject to sort memory limits and can spill to disk. On a view $sample is never first, so it always scans. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample/ · keywords: count, cursor, Count and Distinct and Sampling Optimization
- [passage] If your use case requires a uniform sample, avoid the pseudo-random cursor. To do so, run $sample after another stage, or set N to more than 5% of the documents in the collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample/ · keywords: count, cursor
- [passage] If your use case requires a uniform sample, avoid the pseudo-random cursor. To do so, run [`$sample`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sample) after another stage, or set `N` to more than 5% of the documents in the collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample.md#pseudo-random-cursor-behavior · keywords: count, cursor, $sample
- [passage] `$changeStreamSplitLargeEvent` splits events that exceed 16 MB into fragments and returns the fragments sequentially using the change stream cursor. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/changeStreamSplitLargeEvent.md#behavior · keywords: cursor, $changeStreamSplitLargeEvent
- [fact] estimatedDocumentCount() can be inaccurate after an unclean shutdown (drift depends on writes since the last checkpoint, usually 60 s) and on a sharded cluster does not filter orphaned documents; running validate on each collection restores the count statistic. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.estimatedDocumentCount/ · keywords: count, Count and Distinct and Sampling Optimization

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] | Field | Type | Literal or Normalized | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `key` | Document | Literal | Contains the query shape and additional query attributes that group a set of queries together | | `key.queryShape` | Document | Literal | Contains attributes used to group similar queries together. For more information, see [Query Shape.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querystats.md#std-label-queryStats-queryShape) | | `key.client` | Document | Literal | Describes client information associated with the key | | `key.client.application` | Document | Literal | The client application name | | `key.client.driver` | Document | Literal | Describes the driver used to issue the query | | `key.client.driver.name` | String | Literal | Name of the driver used to issue the query. Possible values include `mongosh` and `nodejs`. | | `key.client.driver.version` | String | Literal | Version number of the driver used to issue the query | | `key.client.os` | Document | Literal | Describes the operating system used by the client that issued the query | | `key.client.os.type` | String | Literal | Type of the operating system | | `key.client.os.name` | String | Literal | Name of the operating system | | `key.client.os.architecture` | String | Literal | Architecture of the operating system. Possible values include `arm64` and `x86_64`. | | `key.client.os.version` | String | Literal | Version number of the operating system | | `key.readConcern` | Document | Literal | The [read concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md#std-label-read-concern) for the key | | `key.collectionType` | String | Literal | The type of collection the query was issued on. For more information, see [Collection Type.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querystats.md#std-label-queryStats-collectionType) | | `key.hint` | Document or String | Normalized | The index that was used as a [hint](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#std-label-cursor-hint) for the query | | `key.batchSize` | String | Normalized | The [batch size](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.batchsize.md#std-label-cursor-batchSize) for the key. Batch size specifies the maximum number of documents that can be returned in each batch of a query result. By default, the initial batch size is the lesser of `101` documents or 16 mebibytes (MiB) worth of documents. Subsequent batches have a maximum size of 16 MiB. `batchSize` can enforce a smaller limit than 16 MiB, but not a larger one. When set, the `batchSize` is the lesser of `batchSize` documents or 16 MiB worth of documents. | | `key.comment` | String | Normalized | Comment associated with the key | | `key.maxTimeMS` | String | Normalized | [maxTimeMS](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#std-label-cursor-maxTimeMS) value associated with the key | | `key.noCursorTimeout` | Boolean | Normalized | [noCursorTimeout](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#std-label-cursor-noCursorTimeout) option associated with the key | | `key.readPreference` | String | Literal | [Read preference](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-preference.md#std-label-read-preference) associated with the key | | `key.apiVersion` | String | Literal | The Stable API version associated with the key. See [MongoDB Stable API for Server Upgrades.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/stable-api.md#std-label-stable-api) | | `key.apiStrict` | Boolean | Literal | The `apiStrict` parameter value associated with the key. See [Stable API Parameters.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/stable-api.md#std-label-stable-api-params) | | `key.apiDeprecationErrors` | Boolean | Literal | The `apiDeprecationErrors` parameter value associated with the key. See [Stable API Parameters.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/stable-api.md#std-label-stable-api-params) | | `keyHash` | String | Literal | A hashed representation of the values in the `key`. Each unique `keyHash` value corresponds to a unique entry in the `$queryStats` memory store. | | `queryShapeHash` | String | Literal | **New in version 8.0** `queryShapeHash` is a hexadecimal string with the hash of a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). For details, see [Query Shapes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) | | `metrics` | Document | Literal | Describes runtime statistics for the key | | `metrics.cursor` | Document | Literal | **New in version 9.0** Metrics related to the cursor and batching protocol | | `metrics``.cursor``.firstResponseExecMicros` | Document | Literal | **Changed in version 9.0** Describes the time spent from when a query within the key began processing to when the server returns the first batch of results All subfields of `firstResponseExecMicros` are reported in microseconds. | | `metrics.queryExec` | Document | Literal | **New in version 9.0** Metrics related to query execution | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsReturned` | Document | Literal | **Changed in version 9.0** Describes the number of documents returned by queries within the key | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsReturned``.sum` | NumberLong | Literal | Total number of documents returned by queries with the given key | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsReturned``.max` | NumberLong | Literal | Maximum number of documents returned by a query with the given key | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsReturned``.min` | NumberLong | Literal | Fewest number of documents returned by a query with the given key | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsReturned``.sumOfSquares` | NumberDecimal | Literal | Sum of squares of number of documents returned by a query within the key. A high `sumOfSquares` value indicates high variance in the number of documents returned between individual queries. | | `metrics``.queryExec``.keysExamined` | Document | Literal | Describes the number of keys examined by queries | | `metrics``.queryExec``.keysExamined``.sum` | Integer | Literal | Total number of keys examined | | `metrics``.queryExec``.keysExamined``.max` | NumberLong | Literal | Maximum number of keys examined | | `metrics``.queryExec``.keysExamined``.min` | NumberLong | Literal | Fewest number of keys examined | | `metrics``.queryExec``.keysExamined``.sumOfSquares` | NumberDecimal | Literal | Sum of squares of number of keys examined. A high `sumOfSquares` value indicates high variance in the number of keys examined in individual queries. | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsExamined` | Document | Literal | **Changed in version 9.0** Describes the number of documents examined by queries | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsExamined``.sum` | Integer | Literal | Total number of documents examined in the query | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsExamined``.max` | NumberLong | Literal | Maximum number of documents examined | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsExamined``.min` | NumberLong | Literal | Minimum number of documents examined | | `metrics``.queryExec``.docsExamined``.sumOfSquares` | NumberDecimal | Literal | Sum of squares of number of documents examined. - [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `count` | string | The name of the collection or view to count. | | `query` | document | Optional. A query that selects which documents to count in the collection or view. | | `limit` | integer | Optional. The maximum number of matching documents to return. | | `skip` | integer | Optional. The number of matching documents to skip before returning results. | | `hint` | string or document | Optional. The index to use. Specify either the index name as a string or the index specification document. | | `readConcern` | document | Optional. Specifies the [read concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-read-concern). The option has the following syntax: `readConcern: { level: <value> }` Possible read concern levels are: [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-). This is the default read concern level for read operations against the primary and secondaries.; [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-). Available for read operations against the primary and secondaries. [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-) behaves the same as [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-) against the primary and non-sharded secondaries. The query returns the instance's most recent data.; [`"majority"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-majority.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-majority-). Available for replica sets that use [WiredTiger storage engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-storage-wiredtiger); [`"linearizable"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-). Available for read operations on the [`primary`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-states.md#mongodb-replstate-replstate.PRIMARY) only.; [`"snapshot"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-snapshot-). Available for [multi-document transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions) and certain read operations outside of multi-document transactions. For more formation on the read concern levels, see [Read Concern Levels.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md#std-label-read-concern-levels) | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds. If you do not specify a value for `maxTimeMS`, operations will not time out. A value of `0` explicitly specifies the default unbounded behavior. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their allotted time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp). MongoDB only terminates an operation at one of its designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) | | `collation` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md#command-fields · keywords: count, cursor, index, read preference, query, limit · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.count.md

- [passage] | Name | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | --clusterName | string | true | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. | | --commands | & | false | Retrieve query shape statistics matching specified MongoDB commands. The currently supported parameters are: find, distinct, aggregate, count, insert, update, and delete. The insert, update, and delete commands return results only for clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later with write query shape statistics enabled for the project. Omit this parameter to return results for all supported commands. | | --envelope | envelope | false | Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an envelope JSON object. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. | | -h, --help | | false | help for listQueryShapeSummaries | | --nSummaries | int | false | Maximum number of query statistic summaries to return. | | --namespaces | . | false | Namespaces from which to retrieve query shape statistics. If you specify the **until** parameter, you must specify the **since** parameter.; If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours. | | --version | string | false | API version to use when calling the Atlas API endpoints [options: "2025-03-12"].
